title: Qwen3.6-27B FP8 on vLLM: 7.8 tok/s bare, ~2x with MTP=3 on Spark
slug_note: The dense-27B reality check on Spark: 7.8 tok/s without speculative decoding, 14.5-15.8 with MTP=3 — and the reason the directory pushes MoE on this box.

engine.config: --speculative-config method=mtp num_speculative_tokens=3 for the doubled rows

requirements.notes: Fits easily; bandwidth, not capacity, is the wall for dense 27B.

steps: Serve Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 with stock vLLM on one Spark
Bench the two prompts below with and without the MTP speculative config

measurements.method: 'write me a commented quicksort function in Python', baseline without MTP
'2-page essay on phone addiction', baseline without MTP
same quicksort prompt with MTP num_speculative_tokens=3
same essay prompt with MTP=3; 15.2 tok/s average across prompts

caveats: A deliberate negative result: keep it visible so 'just run the dense 27B' comes with its number attached.
The thread's qualitative AgentBench note — dense BF16 Qwen3.6 beating MoE quants on agent tasks — is a quality signal, not recorded as a metric here.
